obligations.behavior: Every verb supports --json and has an explain entry; mutating verbs make no change without --apply; 'teken cli doctor --strict' passes

obligations.behavior: scan-secrets.py is clean; only *.example config is tracked; .env, keys and secrets are gitignored

obligations.behavior: push_file, list_library and send_to_device work from an mcp SDK client with an API key; without a key they are refused
obligations.source_text: MCP server exposes push_file / list_library / send_to_device (queue for device) over the same core as the API; culture-rules calls it via MCP or a CodeRunner argv step (xteink library add ... --apply)

obligations.behavior: On Wi-Fi join the device fetches its queue, stores each book on microSD, verifies sha256 before ACK, and reads offline afterwards
obligations.source_text: Device sync pulls from the xteink server (OPDS feed and/or a small JSON 'queue' endpoint) on Wi-Fi join; books land on the microSD and reading never touches the network

obligations.behavior: MCP push_file -> book on device <= 60 s after Wi-Fi join; >= 10 pages read in airplane mode

obligations.behavior: After reboot, all services healthy <= 120 s with no manual step; anon -> SSO, keyless API over tunnel -> 401
obligations.source_text: After a host reboot, all compose services (api+web, mcp, cloudflared) are healthy within 120 s with no manual step, and https://ebooks.culture.dev returns the SSO wall for an anonymous browser and 401 for an API call without a key

obligations.behavior: Fork CI builds all Xteink envs; xteink CI test/web/lint green with coverage >= 60%
obligations.source_text: CI builds every Xteink firmware env (X3/X4 C3, X4Pro, X4C) in the fork repo, and the xteink repo's test, web and lint jobs pass with coverage >= 60%

obligations.behavior: With the tunnel profile off, the stack's test suite + a fake-device sync pass on an egress-denied network (0 outbound connections)
obligations.source_text: Privacy: with the tunnel off, the stack makes 0 outbound connections other than to the device LAN (no telemetry), verified by a network-namespace/egress test

obligations.behavior: Without --profile remote, no cloudflared container runs
obligations.source_text: Tunnel is opt-in: compose profile 'remote' runs cloudflared; without it nothing is reachable from outside the LAN

obligations.behavior: git diff against upstream develop touches only theme/UI, input, Wi-Fi/sync config, sync client, OTA URL and TLS verification
obligations.source_text: Firmware fork keeps upstream CrossPoint's reader engine (EPUB layout, fonts, SD, power) untouched where possible; our changes are theme/UI, button map/zoom, saved-network config and the xteink sync client, to keep upstream merges cheap

obligations.behavior: Versioned contract: auth by device key, queue fetch, download, sha256 ACK; unknown protocol version -> explicit error; identical over LAN and xteink.culture.dev
obligations.source_text: Device sync contract (versioned, documented in docs/device-protocol.md): device authenticates with a per-device key, GETs its queue (book id, title, size, sha256, url), downloads each to microSD, verifies sha256, ACKs; server marks delivered. Works identically over LAN IP and ebooks.culture.dev

obligations.behavior: Upload, library browse/search/delete, send-to-device with status, device pairing, settings each pass a Playwright flow against the compose stack
obligations.source_text: Web UI flows: (1) upload by drag-drop with format check, (2) library browse/search/delete, (3) send-to-device queue with delivery status, (4) devices: pair (show device key/QR), last seen, (5) settings: tunnel status and API keys. Designed with frontend-design, verified by Playwright flows

obligations.behavior: A >= 5 MB EPUB downloads over HTTPS from xteink.culture.dev on the X3 without OOM or watchdog reset
obligations.source_text: Firmware sync client supports HTTPS (TLS) to xteink.culture.dev within ESP32-C3 RAM limits (no PSRAM on X3/X4), since the hotspot fallback goes through the tunnel; upstream already runs TLS on C3 via wolfSSL

obligations.behavior: Sync against a MITM proxy with an untrusted cert fails closed; against xteink.culture.dev it succeeds
obligations.source_text: Firmware verifies the server certificate on every HTTPS sync: replace upstream's http.setInsecure() (src/network/HttpDownloader.cpp:36) with a pinned CA bundle for xteink.culture.dev's Cloudflare edge chain, so the device key cannot be MITM'd on a hotspot

obligations.behavior: OTA check on the fork never offers an upstream CrossPoint release
obligations.source_text: Fork repoints OTA (upstream src/network/OtaUpdater.cpp:22 hardcodes api.github.com/repos/crosspoint-reader/crosspoint-reader/releases/latest) to the fork's own releases, or disables it, so an on-device 'update' never silently replaces our firmware with stock CrossPoint

obligations.behavior: 'xteink device backup --apply' writes a full-flash dump with sha256 before first flash; restore procedure documented and rehearsed once
obligations.source_text: Before the first flash of any unit, 'xteink device backup --port ... --apply' dumps the full stock flash (esptool read-flash) to the server's private store, and docs give the restore path (esptool write-flash / crosspoint-tools boot repair)

obligations.behavior: Two remote-login setups exist: ebooks.culture.dev with Access allow-policy, xteink.culture.dev with --no-access; both route to the same origin
obligations.source_text: Remote access uses two cultureflare hostnames: 'remote-login setup --hostname ebooks.culture.dev --allow <owner email>' (Access SSO, web UI) and 'remote-login setup --hostname xteink.culture.dev --no-access' (device endpoints; xteink enforces the device key), both in front of the same origin

obligations.behavior: Zoom steps snap to available point sizes; reflow happens once on leaving zoom mode; the same passage remains on screen
obligations.source_text: Zoom = reader font point size: built-in fonts offer 12/14/16/18 pt, vector fonts 8-22 pt (upstream src/ReaderFontSizes.h). The zoom scale shows these steps; re-layout happens once when zoom mode exits (not per press), and position/progress is kept by reading position (percent/chapter offset), not page number, since reflow renumbers pages

obligations.behavior: Deleting a delivered book removes the unmodified device copy only for mirror devices; low SD space -> refusal before download; revoked key -> 401
obligations.source_text: Lifecycle: removing a book from the server's device queue/library removes it from the device on next sync only if the device-side copy is unmodified (opt-in 'mirror' per device); low-SD-space is reported to the server and blocks the download instead of failing mid-write; a lost device's key is revocable from CLI/web

obligations.seam: device status API + device home screen
obligations.behavior: Server exposes last_seen, last sync result and queue per device (API, CLI --json, web); device shows a one-line sync status
obligations.source_text: Observability: the server records per-device last_seen, last sync result and queue state (visible in web UI and 'xteink device list --json'); the device shows a one-line sync status (ok / n new / error code) on the home screen

obligations.behavior: Oversized file, wrong magic bytes and EPUB zip bomb are all rejected with 4xx on every upload path
obligations.source_text: Upload containment: size cap, magic-byte/format check, EPUB zip-bomb guard (max entries/uncompressed size), timeout-bounded conversion subprocesses; applies equally to web, API and MCP uploads

obligations.behavior: API/MCP reachable via LAN and tailnet IPs with key; through the tunnel only /api/device/* is routed, any other path -> 404
obligations.source_text: The API/MCP listener is reachable from the LAN and the Tailscale/mesh interfaces of spark (not just 127.0.0.1), while the tunnel ingress for xteink.culture.dev routes only /api/device/* to the origin; any other path through the tunnel returns 404

obligations.behavior: A Markdown/HTML article pushed via MCP or web becomes an EPUB tagged kind=article and syncs to and paginates on the X3
obligations.source_text: Articles are first-class: push_file / web upload accept Markdown and HTML articles (with title/author metadata) and convert them to EPUB (c78), listed alongside books with a kind=article tag
